title: Acharei Mot: not at all times (Leviticus 16:2)
hook: even the high priest may enter the holiest place only once a year

segments.voice: Yesterday, Acharei Mot began with Aaron's loss. Your line was after grief, atonement. Today, the first rule of the Day of Atonement, and the end of a week.

We live in an age of always. Stores open all night. Messages at three in the morning. Every show, every song, every person a tap away, any hour. The idea that something should be off limits most of the time can feel almost foreign. The first instruction Moses receives for Yom Kippur isn't about what Aaron should do. It's about what he shouldn't. The high priest, who wears the golden plate engraved holy to the LORD, is told there's a room he may not simply walk into.
screen: `OPEN ALL NIGHT.` → `THE FIRST RULE IS A NO.` → `A ROOM HE CAN'T WALK INTO.`

segments.voice: The verse, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: tell Aaron "that he come not at all times into the holy place within the veil." Behind that curtain is the holy of holies, the ark and its cover. The chapter goes on to describe one day, the tenth of the seventh month, when the high priest goes in, with incense and blood, on behalf of everyone. Only that day. Some readers draw a lesson: the closer you are to the center, the more the limits matter. There's care inside the limit, too. The Mishnah describes the high priest coming out of the holy of holies and saying a short prayer in the outer room. Short, it says, so as not to frighten the people waiting outside. The limit isn't coldness; everyone outside is holding their breath for him. Look back at the week. Metzora opened with the priest going out of the camp. Then cedar and hyssop, a bird set free, a house emptied before the verdict, and a person walked home step by step. Acharei Mot began with grief before atonement. And now: not at all times. Jewish life is full of these boundaries. Shabbat closes the week's work at sundown. Some things are kept for one night a year. Some find the limit is what keeps a thing precious. A door you can open any time can stop being a door.
screen: `NOT AT ALL TIMES, BEHIND THE VEIL.` · `ONE DAY A YEAR.` · `A SHORT PRAYER, NOT TO FRIGHTEN.` · `A WEEK FROM CAMP TO SANCTUARY.` · then, large: `NOT AT ALL TIMES.`

segments.voice: Think of something that would mean more if it weren't available all the time: your phone at the dinner table, work email after dark, a conversation you keep reopening. Choose one limit you could keep, just for this evening, and picture the door closing gently, and what might have room to grow on the other side of it.
Acharei Mot. The portion where even the high priest may enter the holiest place only on one day a year.
Your line: not at all times. Even the high priest waited for his day. That's the week.

howItsDone: On Yom Kippur, the Musaf service in traditional synagogues retells the high priest's service in the holy of holies, called the Avodah, and Shabbat rest is another limit that sets time apart.

chat.says: Why couldn't the high priest go into the holiest room whenever he wanted?
options: He was told not at all times; he went in only on Yom Kippur, for everyone.
He could, but only after Shabbat ended each week, with incense.
He went in daily, but only the high priest's sons could watch.
chat.meaning: Leviticus 16:2 says he may not come at all times within the veil; only on the tenth of the seventh month does he go in.

holy of holies.meaning: the innermost room behind the veil, where the ark stood

Mishnah.meaning: the early rabbis' collection of Jewish law and teaching

Shabbat.meaning: the seventh day, the day of rest

Acharei Mot.meaning: after the death; the portion with the Yom Kippur service

notes: JPS 1917 Lev 16:2 'that he come not at all times into the holy place within the veil' quoted from memory; confirm.
Mishnah Yoma 5:1: short prayer in the outer sanctuary so as not to alarm Israel; confirm.
The tzitz (golden plate) inscription 'holy to the Lord' (Exodus 28:36) is paraphrased in the hook.

On Yom Kippur the high priest entered the holy of holies more than once that day (Mishnah Yoma); the script says 'only that day', not 'only once'. The index hook says 'only once a year'; kept as the title's sense.
